units.name: 01 Nature vs. Nurture
units.passage: Scientists once drew a clear line between what we inherit from our parents and what we learn from the world around us, and this line has shifted greatly over time. For most of the last century, experts believed that our actions were shaped only by our surroundings, such as family, school, and friends. Today, however, researchers agree that our genes also have a strong effect on the way we behave. Still, the real situation is far more complex than either of these older views. It is very hard to measure how genes and surroundings work together. Consider a common finding: kids who spend time with rough, aggressive friends tend to become more aggressive too. At first, this seems to prove that friends shape behavior. But we should first ask a deeper question: why did these kids pick such friends in the first place? Their choice of friends may simply mirror their own inborn traits. In that case, the friends do not create the aggression; they only awaken tendencies that already existed or make existing aggressive behavior stronger.

items.q: 글의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 사람의 행동은 오로지 환경에 의해 결정된다.
유전자는 사람의 행동에 거의 영향을 주지 않는다.
유전과 환경이 행동에 미치는 영향은 서로 얽혀 있어 단순하게 판단하기 어렵다.
공격적인 친구와 어울리면 누구나 반드시 공격적으로 변한다.
아이의 친구 관계는 부모가 정해 주어야 한다.
items.exp: 옛 관점들보다 실제 상황이 훨씬 복잡하고(far more complex), 유전자와 환경의 상호작용은 측정하기 어렵다는 것이 글의 핵심이에요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 지난 세기 대부분 동안 전문가들은 유전자가 행동을 결정한다고 믿었다.
오늘날 연구자들은 유전자도 행동에 강한 영향을 준다고 본다.
유전자와 환경이 함께 작용하는 방식은 측정하기 매우 어렵다.
공격적인 친구와 지내는 아이들은 더 공격적이 되는 경향이 있다.
아이들이 친구를 고르는 것은 타고난 특성을 반영할 수 있다.
items.exp: 지난 세기 전문가들은 행동이 오직 환경(surroundings)에 의해 만들어진다고 믿었다고 했어요.

items.q: 글쓴이에 따르면, 공격적인 친구가 아이에게 하는 역할로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 아이의 공격성을 처음으로 만들어 낸다.
아이의 공격성을 줄여 준다.
부모의 양육 태도를 바꾼다.
아이에게 새로운 친구를 소개한다.
이미 있던 성향을 깨우거나 더 강하게 만든다.
items.exp: 친구들은 공격성을 만들어 내는 게 아니라 이미 있던 성향을 깨우거나(awaken) 더 강하게 할 뿐이라고 했어요.

items.q: 지문의 문장 'Their choice of friends may simply mirror their own inborn traits.'에서 mirror의 의미로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: to hide completely
to reflect or show
to make larger
to break into pieces
to replace with something else
items.exp: 친구 선택이 타고난 특성을 '반영한다, 보여 준다'는 뜻이므로 to reflect or show가 알맞아요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
kids [who] spend time with rough, aggressive friends tend to become more aggressive too.
choices: I don't know [who] broke the window.
[Who] is your English teacher?
Tell me [who] you met yesterday.
The girl [who] sits next to me is from Busan.
[Who] do you think will win the game?
items.exp: 지문의 who는 선행사 kids를 꾸미는 주격 관계대명사예요. The girl을 꾸미는 who가 같은 쓰임이고, 나머지는 의문사예요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How to Choose Good Friends for Your Child
Why Family Matters More Than Genes
The History of Genetic Research
Genes or Environment? A Puzzle Harder Than It Looks
Aggression: A Problem Only Schools Can Solve
items.exp: 유전과 환경 어느 한쪽이 아니라 둘의 상호작용이 'far more complex'하다는 내용이므로 두 요인의 수수께끼가 보기보다 어렵다는 제목이 알맞아요.

items.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
choices: Experts in the last century thought genes alone shaped behavior.
The line between what we inherit and what we learn has changed a lot over time.
Researchers today deny that genes influence behavior.
Measuring how genes and surroundings interact is simple.
Scientists have never studied children's friendships.
items.exp: 첫 문장에서 유전과 학습을 나누는 선이 'has shifted greatly over time'이라고 했어요. 지난 세기 전문가들은 환경만을 믿었고, 상호작용 측정은 매우 어렵다고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Although older views credited either (A) ___ or genes alone, the writer says their effects are (B) ___ to separate, as the case of aggressive friends shows.
choices: (A) surroundings — (B) easy
(A) friends — (B) pleasant
(A) surroundings — (B) hard
(A) teachers — (B) simple
(A) schools — (B) quick
items.exp: 옛 관점은 행동이 'only by our surroundings'로 만들어진다고 보았고, 글쓴이는 'It is very hard to measure how genes and surroundings work together'라고 했어요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [drew a clear line between]이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (Scientists once [drew a clear line between] what we inherit from our parents and what we learn from the world around us, and this line has shifted greatly over time.)
choices: 두 가지를 서로 완전히 별개의 것으로 구분했다
두 가지를 측정하는 도구를 발명했다
두 가지가 함께 작용한다고 인정했다
두 가지 중 어느 것도 중요하지 않다고 보았다
두 가지를 종이에 그림으로 그렸다
items.exp: 'draw a line between A and B'는 A와 B를 뚜렷이 구분한다는 뜻이에요. 뒤에서 이 구분이 바뀌고 실제로는 둘이 얽혀 있다고 하므로, 예전에는 유전과 환경을 별개로 나누었다는 의미예요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: this line has [shifted] greatly over time
our actions were [shaped] only by our surroundings
have a [strong] effect on the way we behave
the real situation is far more [complex]
this seems to [disprove] that friends shape behavior
items.exp: 공격적인 친구와 지내는 아이가 더 공격적이 되는 현상은 언뜻 친구가 행동을 만든다는 것을 '증명하는(prove)' 듯 보인다고 해야 자연스러워요. 원문은 'this seems to prove that friends shape behavior'예요.

units.name: 02 Use of Fire
units.passage: Richard Wrangham, in his book Catching Fire, argues that fire completely changed the way our early ancestors lived. When one pound of firewood burns, it can give off as much as 1,600 kcal of energy. In an ordinary campfire, much of this heat simply escapes into the air. However, the part of the energy that food takes in during cooking alters the food's chemical makeup and structure, so our bodies can digest it more easily. For example, heat softens meat, breaks proteins apart, and turns starches that we could not digest into carbohydrates that we can. This change is easy to see in root vegetables, because some of the starches in them cannot be digested by the human body. A cooked potato gives us about two times as many calories as an uncooked one. Basically, fire brought about a revolution in the diet of early humans. It packed more energy into every mouthful, and at the same time, it cut down the energy their bodies needed to spend on digestion.

items.q: 글의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 캠프파이어는 열에너지를 대부분 낭비하므로 비효율적이다.
익힌 음식은 날음식보다 소화하기 어렵다.
뿌리채소는 날것으로 먹을 때 영양가가 가장 높다.
인류는 불을 발견한 뒤 고기만 먹게 되었다.
불로 조리하면서 음식에서 얻는 에너지는 늘고 소화 부담은 줄어 인류의 식생활이 크게 바뀌었다.
items.exp: 마지막 부분에서 불이 한 입당 에너지를 늘리고 소화에 드는 에너지를 줄여 식단에 혁명을 일으켰다고 정리하고 있어요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 캠프파이어의 열은 대부분 음식에 흡수된다.
장작 1파운드는 최대 1,600kcal의 에너지를 낼 수 있다.
조리하면 녹말이 소화되지 않는 형태로 바뀐다.
익힌 감자는 날감자보다 칼로리가 절반이다.
불은 소화에 쓰이는 에너지를 늘렸다.
items.exp: 장작 1파운드가 탈 때 1,600kcal까지(as much as) 에너지를 낼 수 있다고 했어요.

items.q: 조리할 때 음식에 일어나는 변화로 언급되지 않은 것은?
choices: 고기가 부드러워진다.
단백질이 분해된다.
소화되지 않던 녹말이 탄수화물로 바뀐다.
음식 속 수분의 양이 늘어난다.
음식의 화학적 성질과 구조가 바뀐다.
items.exp: 고기가 부드러워지고, 단백질이 분해되고, 녹말이 탄수화물로 바뀌며, 화학적 성질과 구조가 바뀐다고 했지만 수분 이야기는 없어요.

items.q: 지문의 'heat softens meat'에서 softens와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: makes tender
makes tough
makes cold
makes dry
makes heavy
items.exp: soften은 '부드럽게 하다'라는 뜻이므로 makes tender(연하게 만들다)와 의미가 같아요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
A [cooked] potato gives us about two times as many calories as an uncooked one.
choices: She is [cooking] dinner now.
I have [cooked] for my family many times.
We bought a [used] car last year.
He [cooked] pasta last night.
[Boiling] water is very hot.
items.exp: cooked는 명사 potato를 꾸미며 '익혀진'이라는 수동의 뜻을 가진 과거분사예요. car를 꾸미는 used(사용된)가 같은 쓰임이에요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How to Build a Safe Campfire
Why Raw Vegetables Are Healthier
The Dangers of Burning Firewood
Richard Wrangham's Life Story
Cooking with Fire: More Energy from Every Bite
items.exp: 불로 조리하면 'It packed more energy into every mouthful'이라고 하며 식단의 혁명을 설명하는 글이므로, 한 입마다 더 많은 에너지를 얻게 되었다는 제목이 알맞아요.

items.q: Why does the writer mention root vegetables?
choices: Because they contain no starch at all.
Because they were the only food early humans ate.
Because some of their starches cannot be digested by humans, so cooking's effect is easy to see.
Because they lose most of their calories when cooked.
Because they burn well as firewood.
items.exp: 뿌리채소 속 일부 녹말은 사람 몸이 소화하지 못하기 때문에(some of the starches in them cannot be digested) 조리의 효과가 'easy to see'하다고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Cooking with fire changes the (A) ___ of food, so humans gain more (B) ___ from it while spending less effort on digestion.
choices: (A) structure — (B) energy
(A) color — (B) water
(A) price — (B) time
(A) taste — (B) calories
(A) smell — (B) weight
items.exp: 조리할 때 흡수된 에너지가 'alters the food's chemical makeup and structure'하고, 그 결과 'packed more energy into every mouthful'이라고 했어요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [It packed more energy into every mouthful]이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? ([It packed more energy into every mouthful], and at the same time, it cut down the energy their bodies needed to spend on digestion.)
choices: 음식을 한 번에 더 많이 먹게 되었다
음식의 전체 양이 줄어들었다
음식이 더 뜨거워져 먹기 어려워졌다
같은 양의 음식에서 더 많은 열량을 얻게 되었다
사람들이 음식을 더 빨리 씹게 되었다
items.exp: 'A cooked potato gives us about two times as many calories as an uncooked one'처럼, 한 입(mouthful)마다 더 많은 에너지가 담기게 되었다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문장을 옮긴 것으로 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: fire completely [changed] the way our early ancestors lived
some of the starches in them cannot [digest] by the human body
much of this heat simply [escapes] into the air
so our bodies can [digest] it more easily
it cut down the energy their bodies [needed] to spend
items.exp: 녹말이 사람 몸에 의해 '소화되는' 것이므로 수동태 'cannot be digested by the human body'가 되어야 해요. by 뒤에 행위자가 있는 것도 수동태의 단서예요.

units.name: 03 Verbal Ping-Pong
units.passage: To build real bonds with others through talking, think of conversation as a game of ping-pong played with words. Because I enjoy talking so much, I often pause and ask myself whether the other person has had enough turns to hit the ball. If they haven't, I admit right away that I have been talking mostly about myself and tell them I would really like to hear what is going on in their lives. But this has to be sincere. Speaking about yourself for sixty minutes and then saying, "Oh, I have to leave — how have you been?" will not do the job. Firing question after question about the other person while revealing nothing about yourself does not work either. For others to feel close to you, they need to learn about your life, too: how things are going, what plans you have, and what you have been feeling lately. If you only ask questions and keep yourself hidden, the other person might think you are interested in them, but they will not feel a real bond with you.

items.q: 글쓴이의 주장으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 대화에서는 상대방의 말을 끝까지 들어 주기만 하면 된다.
대화로 친밀감을 쌓으려면 말할 기회를 주고받으며 자신의 이야기도 나눠야 한다.
상대에게 질문을 많이 할수록 더 친해질 수 있다.
친한 사이일수록 대화 시간을 짧게 해야 한다.
대화 주제는 미리 준비해 두는 것이 좋다.
items.exp: 대화를 탁구처럼 주고받아야 하고, 질문만 하지 말고 내 근황과 감정도 나눠야 진짜 유대감이 생긴다고 주장해요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 글쓴이는 말하는 것을 아주 좋아한다.
글쓴이는 대화 중에 상대방이 충분히 말했는지 스스로 점검한다.
자기 얘기만 오래 하다가 마지막에 안부를 묻는 것은 충분하지 않다.
상대방에 대해 질문만 계속하면 깊은 유대감을 느끼게 할 수 있다.
다른 사람이 가까움을 느끼려면 나의 근황과 감정도 알아야 한다.
items.exp: 질문만 하고 자신을 숨기면 상대는 관심은 느껴도 진짜 유대감(a real bond)은 느끼지 못한다고 했어요.

items.q: 지문의 'whether the other person has had enough turns to hit the ball'이 의미하는 바로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 상대방이 말할 기회를 충분히 가졌는지
상대방이 탁구를 잘 치는지
대화 주제가 다양했는지
상대방이 내 말에 동의했는지
대화가 충분히 길었는지
items.exp: 대화를 탁구에 비유했으므로 공을 칠 차례(turns)는 상대방이 말할 기회를 뜻해요.

items.q: 지문의 'But this has to be sincere.'에서 sincere와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: polite
funny
honest and real
quick
careful
items.exp: 겉으로만 안부를 묻는 것은 안 된다고 이어지므로 sincere는 '진심 어린, 진실한'이라는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
[Speaking] about yourself for sixty minutes and then saying, "Oh, I have to leave — how have you been?" will not do the job.
choices: The boy [speaking] to Mina is my brother.
She is [speaking] on the phone now.
[Speaking] loudly, he walked into the room.
I heard someone [speaking] outside.
[Speaking] in front of many people is hard for me.
items.exp: 지문의 Speaking은 문장의 주어 역할을 하는 동명사예요. 주어로 쓰인 마지막 문장의 Speaking이 같은 쓰임이고, 나머지는 분사나 진행형이에요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Conversation as Ping-Pong: Give and Take to Build Bonds
How to Win Every Argument
Why Listening Is All You Need
The Secret of Asking Good Questions
Talking Less, Living Better
items.exp: 대화를 'a game of ping-pong played with words'에 비유해 서로 주고받아야 진짜 유대감이 생긴다는 글이에요. 듣기만 하거나 질문만 하는 것은 안 된다고 했으므로 나머지는 맞지 않아요.

items.q: What does the writer do when he realizes the other person has not had enough turns to talk?
choices: He ends the conversation politely.
He changes the topic to something lighter.
He asks them to say more about him.
He admits he has been talking about himself and says he wants to hear about their life.
He keeps talking until he finishes his story.
items.exp: 상대가 충분히 말하지 못했다면 'I admit right away that I have been talking mostly about myself and tell them I would really like to hear what is going on in their lives'라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

To form a true connection, a conversation should be (A) ___, with both people taking turns and the speaker also (B) ___ things about himself or herself.
choices: (A) short — (B) hiding
(A) one-sided — (B) sharing
(A) balanced — (B) hiding
(A) formal — (B) forgetting
(A) balanced — (B) sharing
items.exp: 탁구처럼 차례(turns)를 주고받고, 'they need to learn about your life, too'라고 했으므로 균형 잡힌 대화와 자기 이야기 나누기가 핵심이에요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [will not do the job]이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (Speaking about yourself for sixty minutes and then saying, "Oh, I have to leave — how have you been?" [will not do the job].)
choices: 직장에서 맡은 업무를 끝내지 못한다
진심 어린 관심을 보여 주지 못해 유대감을 만들 수 없다
대화를 너무 짧게 끝내게 된다
상대방을 화나게 만들어 떠나게 한다
질문을 너무 많이 하게 된다
items.exp: 바로 앞에서 'this has to be sincere'라고 했으므로, 떠나기 직전에 형식적으로 안부를 묻는 것은 진심이 아니어서 유대감을 쌓는 역할을 하지 못한다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: think of conversation as a [game] of ping-pong
I [admit] right away that I have been talking
the other person might think you are [uninterested] in them
while [revealing] nothing about yourself does not work either
they need to [learn] about your life, too
items.exp: 질문만 하면 상대는 당신이 자기에게 '관심이 있다(interested)'고 생각할 수는 있지만 진짜 유대감은 느끼지 못한다는 흐름이에요. 원문은 'you are interested in them'이에요.

units.name: 04 Leadership
units.passage: A good leader builds a setting in which every member of a team can develop. Such a leader also makes sure that the basic conditions are equal for all, no matter whether a person has a lot of experience or very little. Within this shared setting, the leader plants seeds and takes care of them, while keeping in mind that some people require extra care before they can settle in and start to develop. The leader offers kindness, attention, help, and guidance in the amount that fits each individual. Think about how a gardener works. A gardener would never spread manure on roses. Why not? Manure is too powerful for such a delicate flower, and it would kill it. On the other hand, for a tougher plant like an apple tree, the same manure might be exactly what it needs. Of course, I do not mean that manure is a useful tool for helping people grow. My point is that people are not all the same, so each one needs a way of support that suits them and draws out their best.

items.q: 글쓴이의 주장으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 리더는 모든 구성원을 똑같은 방식으로 대해야 한다.
리더는 경험 많은 구성원에게 더 많은 기회를 줘야 한다.
리더는 구성원 간의 갈등을 먼저 해결해야 한다.
리더는 구성원 각자의 특성에 맞는 방식으로 성장을 도와야 한다.
리더는 정원 가꾸기처럼 꾸준한 취미를 가져야 한다.
items.exp: 마지막 문장에서 사람은 모두 달라서 각자에게 맞고 최선을 끌어내는 지원 방식이 필요하다고 주장해요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 좋은 리더는 경험이 많은 사람에게 더 좋은 환경을 준다.
모든 사람은 같은 양의 보살핌이 필요하다.
장미에 거름을 주면 장미가 죽을 수 있다.
사과나무에는 거름을 주면 안 된다.
글쓴이는 거름이 사람을 키우는 좋은 방법이라고 말한다.
items.exp: 거름은 장미처럼 연약한 꽃에는 너무 강해서 꽃을 죽일 수 있다고 했어요.

items.q: 글에서 정원사의 예가 말하고자 하는 바로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 장미는 사과나무보다 키우기 쉽다.
같은 도움도 대상에 따라 해가 되거나 득이 될 수 있다.
거름은 모든 식물에 해롭다.
식물은 사람보다 보살핌이 덜 필요하다.
정원사는 리더보다 더 중요한 역할을 한다.
items.exp: 같은 거름이 장미에게는 해롭지만 사과나무에게는 딱 필요한 것일 수 있다는 예로, 사람마다 맞는 도움이 다르다는 점을 보여 줘요.

items.q: 지문의 'such a delicate flower'에서 delicate의 영영 풀이로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: very large and heavy
strong and hardy
having a bad smell
growing very fast
easily damaged or hurt
items.exp: 거름이 너무 강해 꽃을 죽일 수 있고, 뒤에서 더 튼튼한(tougher) 사과나무와 대비되므로 delicate는 '연약한'이라는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]과 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 것은?
the basic conditions are equal for all, [no matter whether] a person has a lot of experience or very little.
choices: regardless of whether
because
so that
unless
as soon as
items.exp: no matter whether A or B는 'A든 B든 상관없이'라는 양보의 뜻으로 regardless of whether와 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Why Roses Need More Manure
Leading Like a Gardener: Different Care for Different People
Equal Treatment: The Only Fair Leadership
How to Grow Apple Trees Successfully
Experience Matters Most in a Team
items.exp: 정원사가 식물마다 다르게 돌보듯, 'each one needs a way of support that suits them'이라는 리더십을 말하는 글이에요.

items.q: According to the passage, what does a good leader keep in mind while caring for the team?
choices: Only experienced members deserve the leader's attention.
Every member should receive exactly the same amount of help.
Delicate members should be removed from the team.
Kindness should be saved for the leader's favorites.
Some people need extra care before they can settle in and start to develop.
items.exp: 리더는 'some people require extra care before they can settle in and start to develop'라는 점을 염두에 둔다고 했어요. 도움의 양은 'in the amount that fits each individual'이에요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

A good leader provides (A) ___ conditions for everyone but adjusts the kind and amount of support to fit each (B) ___.
choices: (A) harsh — (B) plant
(A) equal — (B) season
(A) unequal — (B) individual
(A) equal — (B) individual
(A) secret — (B) gardener
items.exp: 기본 조건은 'equal for all'이지만, 친절·관심·도움은 'in the amount that fits each individual'로 준다고 했어요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [plants seeds and takes care of them]이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (Within this shared setting, the leader [plants seeds and takes care of them], while keeping in mind that some people require extra care before they can settle in and start to develop.)
choices: 팀의 정원에 실제로 식물을 심어 가꾼다
구성원을 경험에 따라 둘로 나눈다
구성원이 성장할 수 있도록 기회를 주고 꾸준히 도움을 준다
팀의 실수를 숨기고 보호한다
구성원들에게 농사일을 가르친다
items.exp: 리더를 정원사에, 구성원을 식물에 비유한 표현이에요. 씨를 심고 돌보는 것은 구성원이 'settle in and start to develop'할 수 있게 돕는 것을 뜻해요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문장을 옮긴 것으로 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: a way of support that [suit] them
a setting in [which] every member of a team can develop
makes sure that the basic conditions [are] equal for all
some people [require] extra care before they can settle in
A gardener would never [spread] manure on roses
items.exp: 관계대명사 that의 선행사가 단수 명사 'a way of support'이므로 동사도 3인칭 단수 'suits'가 되어야 해요. 원문은 'a way of support that suits them and draws out their best'예요.

units.name: 05 Consumer Spending
units.passage: Jeanne Boeh, an economist at Augsburg College, says that Americans buy far more goods today than they did in the past. In earlier times, she explains, people without much money could not own things such as air conditioners, televisions, or cell phones. Now, however, even low-income families have them. Boeh believes the main reason is that these products have become cheaper. According to the law of demand, people purchase more of something when its price drops. In addition, we need to work fewer hours to pay for the same item. Cell phones are a clear example. In 1984, a worker with an average income had to work 456 hours to afford one, but today the number is only about four. Of course, households spend more money overall: the average family spent about $48,000 in 2006 and more than $72,000 in 2022. Still, our money generally gets us more than before, so we do not need to feel bad about it. Boeh thinks many of these goods have improved people's lives. Also, since consumer spending accounts for roughly two-thirds of a nation's economic activity, a culture of buying plays a key role in the economy.

items.q: 글의 요지로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 물건이 싸져서 소비가 늘었고, 소비는 삶을 개선하고 경제에도 중요하므로 죄책감을 가질 필요가 없다.
미국인들은 소비를 줄이고 저축을 늘려야 한다.
가난한 사람들은 여전히 기본적인 물건조차 갖기 어렵다.
휴대전화 가격이 오르면서 가계 지출이 크게 늘었다.
소비 문화는 경제에 거의 영향을 주지 않는다.
items.exp: 물건이 싸져 소비가 늘었지만 돈으로 더 많이 얻게 되었으니 죄책감을 느낄 필요가 없고, 소비가 삶을 개선하며 경제에 중요하다는 내용이에요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Boeh는 Augsburg 대학의 경제학자이다.
예전에는 가난한 사람들이 에어컨이나 TV를 갖기 어려웠다.
수요의 법칙에 따르면 가격이 내려가면 더 많이 산다.
평균 가구 지출은 2006년보다 2022년에 더 많았다.
소비자 지출은 한 나라 경제 활동의 약 3분의 1을 차지한다.
items.exp: 소비자 지출은 경제 활동의 약 3분의 2(two-thirds)를 차지한다고 했어요.

items.q: 1984년에 평균 소득의 근로자가 휴대전화 한 대를 사기 위해 일해야 했던 시간은?
choices: 약 4시간
약 48시간
456시간
720시간
items.exp: 1984년에는 456시간을 일해야 휴대전화를 살 수 있었고, 오늘날은 약 4시간이라고 했어요.

items.q: 지문의 'consumer spending accounts for roughly two-thirds of a nation's economic activity'에서 accounts for와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: takes care of
pays for
stays away from
makes up
looks for
items.exp: 소비자 지출이 경제 활동의 약 3분의 2를 '차지한다'는 뜻이므로 makes up과 의미가 같아요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
In 1984, a worker with an average income had to work 456 hours [to afford] one.
choices: I want [to buy] a new phone.
She saved money [to buy] a new bike.
I have a lot of homework [to do] tonight.
It is hard [to wake] up early.
My dream is [to be] a doctor.
items.exp: to afford는 '살 여유를 갖기 위해'라는 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법이에요. 자전거를 사기 위해 돈을 모았다는 문장이 같은 쓰임이에요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: The Rising Cost of Living in America
How Cell Phones Were Invented
Why Buying More Is Not Something to Feel Guilty About
Saving Money: A Forgotten Habit
The Law of Demand Explained for Beginners
items.exp: 물건이 싸져 소비가 늘었지만 'we do not need to feel bad about it'이라고 하며 소비가 삶과 경제에 도움이 된다고 하는 글이에요. 수요의 법칙은 글의 일부 소재일 뿐이에요.

items.q: According to Boeh, what is the main reason even low-income families now own goods like air conditioners?
choices: These products have become cheaper.
Families earn far more money than before.
The government gives such goods away.
Families work much longer hours than before.
Banks lend money more easily.
items.exp: Boeh는 'the main reason is that these products have become cheaper'라고 했어요. 오히려 같은 물건을 사기 위해 일하는 시간은 줄었다고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Because goods have become (A) ___ and take fewer work hours to buy, Americans consume more, and the writer views this spending as (B) ___ to both people's lives and the economy.
choices: (A) cheaper — (B) harmful
(A) cheaper — (B) beneficial
(A) rarer — (B) beneficial
(A) heavier — (B) useless
(A) pricier — (B) dangerous
items.exp: 물건이 'cheaper'해져서 소비가 늘었고, 그 물건들이 'improved people's lives'하며 소비 문화가 경제에서 'a key role'을 한다고 했으므로 긍정적으로 본 거예요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [our money generally gets us more than before]가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (Still, [our money generally gets us more than before], so we do not need to feel bad about it.)
choices: 우리의 소득이 예전보다 크게 올랐다
물건 가격이 예전보다 계속 오르고 있다
사람들이 예전보다 저축을 더 많이 한다
돈이 예전보다 더 빨리 사라진다
같은 돈으로 예전보다 더 많은 물건과 가치를 얻는다
items.exp: 휴대전화를 사는 데 필요한 노동 시간이 456시간에서 약 4시간으로 줄었다는 예처럼, 돈이 예전보다 더 많은 것을 '얻어 준다(gets us more)'는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: Americans buy far [more] goods today than they did
people purchase [more] of something when its price drops
we need to work [fewer] hours to pay for the same item
many of these goods have [worsened] people's lives
households spend [more] money overall
items.exp: 소비에 죄책감을 가질 필요가 없다는 흐름이므로 물건들이 삶을 '개선했다(improved)'고 해야 맞아요. 원문은 'many of these goods have improved people's lives'예요.

units.name: 06 How to Educate
units.passage: Cory, a first-grader, handed in her homework, a page of the letter g, to her teacher, Mr. Tuttle. After looking it over, he asked her which g she liked the most. When Cory showed him her best one, Mr. Tuttle pointed out the one he liked best, too. Next, he pointed to a g that had two tails instead of one and asked whether Cory could correct it on her own. She said yes and returned to her seat to work on it. Mr. Tuttle did not simply mark the mistake. Instead, he began with what Cory had done well and then let her judge her own mistake. This story shows the idea of growing from strengths rather than from weaknesses. Parents and teachers have the duty to help children develop their skills, both in school subjects and in getting along with others. However, encouragement is usually the most powerful way to make a child want to improve. Other methods can also be used, but they work best when the child has already received warm support, because then he or she will be open to them.

items.q: 글쓴이의 주장으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 아이의 실수는 즉시 정확하게 지적해야 한다.
글씨 쓰기는 초등학교 1학년 때 꼭 익혀야 한다.
아이의 약점보다 강점에 먼저 주목하고 격려하는 것이 아이를 발전시키는 가장 좋은 방법이다.
부모보다 교사가 아이 교육에 더 큰 책임이 있다.
아이에게 스스로 고칠 기회를 주는 것은 위험하다.
items.exp: 강점을 바탕으로 키우는 일화를 든 뒤, 격려(encouragement)가 아이가 나아지고 싶게 만드는 가장 강력한 방법이라고 주장해요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Tuttle 선생님은 Cory에게 가장 마음에 드는 g를 먼저 고르게 했다.
Tuttle 선생님이 Cory의 틀린 g를 직접 고쳐 주었다.
Cory는 꼬리가 두 개인 g를 가장 좋아했다.
Cory는 집에 가서 틀린 글자를 고쳤다.
Tuttle 선생님은 Cory의 실수부터 먼저 지적했다.
items.exp: 선생님은 숙제를 살펴본 뒤 Cory에게 어떤 g가 가장 마음에 드는지 먼저 물었어요.

items.q: 꼬리가 두 개인 g에 대한 설명으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Cory가 가장 잘 쓴 글자이다.
다른 학생이 쓴 글자이다.
선생님이 칠판에 쓴 예시 글자이다.
Cory가 처음으로 배운 글자이다.
Cory가 잘못 쓴 글자로, 선생님이 스스로 고쳐 보게 했다.
items.exp: 선생님은 꼬리가 두 개인 g를 가리키며 Cory가 혼자 고칠 수 있는지(correct it on her own) 물었어요.

items.q: 지문의 'he or she will be open to them'에서 open의 의미로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: not closed for business
willing to accept new ideas
not hidden or secret
empty and wide
starting to bloom
items.exp: 따뜻한 지지를 받은 아이는 다른 방법도 '기꺼이 받아들인다'는 뜻이므로 willing to accept new ideas가 알맞아요.

items.q:
다음 문장을 어법상 바르게 고친 것은?
Parents and teachers have the duty to help children [developing] their skills.
choices: have → has
the duty → duty
to help → helping
developing → develop
their → its
items.exp: help는 목적어 뒤에 동사원형이나 to부정사를 쓰므로 developing을 develop으로 고쳐야 해요. 주어가 복수라 have는 맞아요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How to Write the Letter g Correctly
Why Teachers Should Mark Every Mistake
A First-Grader's Difficult Homework
Growing from Strengths: The Power of Encouragement
Parents vs. Teachers: Who Is Responsible?
items.exp: Cory의 일화로 'growing from strengths rather than from weaknesses'를 보여 주고, 'encouragement is usually the most powerful way'라고 하는 글이에요.

items.q: According to the passage, when do other teaching methods work best?
choices: When the teacher marks every mistake first.
When the child has already received warm support.
When the child is punished for errors.
When parents stay out of the child's education.
When the child works entirely alone.
items.exp: 다른 방법들은 'work best when the child has already received warm support'라고 했어요. 그래야 아이가 그 방법들을 받아들이기 때문이에요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Mr. Tuttle's way of starting with Cory's (A) ___ work shows that children improve most when adults (B) ___ them rather than focus on their weaknesses.
choices: (A) worst — (B) encourage
(A) best — (B) criticize
(A) best — (B) encourage
(A) messy — (B) ignore
(A) unfinished — (B) punish
items.exp: 선생님은 'began with what Cory had done well'했고, 글은 'encouragement is usually the most powerful way to make a child want to improve'라고 했어요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [growing from strengths rather than from weaknesses]가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (This story shows the idea of [growing from strengths rather than from weaknesses].)
choices: 잘하는 점을 바탕으로 발전하도록 돕는 것
약한 과목부터 먼저 공부하는 것
운동으로 신체의 힘을 키우는 것
실수를 절대 하지 않도록 훈련하는 것
강한 학생과 약한 학생을 따로 가르치는 것
items.exp: 선생님이 'what Cory had done well'에서 시작한 뒤 실수를 스스로 판단하게 한 것처럼, 아이의 강점을 바탕으로 성장하게 한다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문장을 옮긴 것으로 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: he asked her which g she [liked] the most
whether Cory [could correct] it on her own
the most powerful way to [make] a child want to improve
because then he or she [will be] open to them
then let her [to judge] her own mistake
items.exp: 사역동사 let은 <let+목적어+동사원형>으로 쓰므로 'let her judge'가 맞아요. 원문은 'then let her judge her own mistake'예요.

units.name: 07 Early Adopter
units.passage: Many companies believe that early adopters, the people who buy new gadgets the moment they appear, are the most powerful shoppers in a market. These firms imagine that such buyers understand a product just as well as the engineers who created it and share their excitement about it. For this reason, companies often spend large amounts of money advertising to early adopters through expert magazines, tech blogs, and similar media. However, this may be a poor way to use a limited marketing budget. Studies of well-known technologies, including cell phones, personal computers, GPS navigation systems, and automobiles, suggest that early adopters are so busy testing every feature of their new devices that they hardly affect ordinary buyers, who know far less about technology. In other words, their passion keeps them inside a small circle of fellow fans rather than spreading to the general public. Therefore, businesses should rethink any marketing plan that depends on early adopters to make a product popular. Instead, they need to find better ways to reach the average consumer directly.

items.q: 글쓴이의 주장으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 얼리어답터를 위한 전문 잡지 광고를 늘려야 한다.
얼리어답터에 의존하는 마케팅 전략을 다시 생각해 보아야 한다.
제품 개발자는 소비자의 의견을 더 많이 들어야 한다.
기술 제품은 사용법을 더 쉽게 만들어야 한다.
기업은 신제품 출시 시기를 앞당겨야 한다.
items.exp: Therefore 뒤에서 얼리어답터에 의존해 제품을 인기 있게 만들려는 마케팅 계획을 재고해야 한다(should rethink)고 주장하고 있어요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 많은 기업은 얼리어답터가 시장에서 가장 영향력 있는 소비자라고 생각한다.
기업들은 얼리어답터가 제품을 개발자만큼 잘 안다고 여긴다.
기업들은 전문 잡지나 기술 블로그를 통해 얼리어답터에게 광고한다.
연구에 따르면 얼리어답터는 일반 소비자에게 큰 영향을 준다.
얼리어답터는 새 기기의 모든 기능을 시험해 보느라 바쁘다.
items.exp: 연구 결과 얼리어답터는 기기를 시험하느라 바빠서 일반 소비자에게 거의 영향을 주지 않는다(hardly affect)고 했어요.

items.q: According to the passage, why do early adopters have little effect on ordinary buyers?
choices: They are too busy exploring their new devices.
They cannot afford expensive products.
They refuse to share their opinions online.
They trust only specialist magazines.
They usually buy products later than others.
items.exp: 얼리어답터는 새 기기의 기능을 시험하느라 너무 바빠서(so busy testing every feature) 일반 구매자에게 영향을 거의 주지 못한다고 했어요.

items.q: 지문의 단어 passion과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: anger
patience
doubt
fear
enthusiasm
items.exp: passion은 '열정'이라는 뜻으로, 앞에서 말한 제품에 대한 excitement를 가리키므로 enthusiasm과 의미가 가장 가까워요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
"Early adopters are so busy testing every feature of their new devices [that] they hardly affect ordinary buyers."
choices: I know that she is honest.
This is the book that I bought yesterday.
The box was so heavy that I couldn't lift it.
It is true that he told a lie.
The news that he won the race surprised us.
items.exp: 지문의 that은 <so ~ that ...> '너무 ~해서 …하다' 구문의 결과를 나타내는 that이에요. 같은 쓰임은 'so heavy that I couldn't lift it'이에요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: How to Become an Early Adopter
The History of GPS Navigation
Why Engineers Love New Gadgets
Tech Blogs: The Future of Advertising
Early Adopters: Not the Best Target for Your Marketing Money
items.exp: 얼리어답터에게 광고하는 것이 'a poor way to use a limited marketing budget'일 수 있으니 전략을 다시 생각하라는 글이에요.

items.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
choices: Early adopters wait several months before buying new gadgets.
Companies rarely spend money advertising to early adopters.
The studies covered technologies such as cell phones, personal computers, and automobiles.
Ordinary buyers know more about technology than early adopters.
The writer suggests ignoring the average consumer.
items.exp: 'Studies of well-known technologies, including cell phones, personal computers, GPS navigation systems, and automobiles'라고 했어요. 얼리어답터는 신제품이 나오는 순간(the moment they appear) 구매하고, 일반 구매자는 기술을 훨씬 덜 알아요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Companies expect early adopters to (A) ___ a product's popularity, but since their enthusiasm stays within a small group, firms should aim their marketing at (B) ___ consumers instead.
choices: (A) spread — (B) average
(A) spread — (B) expert
(A) reduce — (B) average
(A) test — (B) wealthy
(A) delay — (B) young
items.exp: 기업은 얼리어답터가 제품을 인기 있게 만들어 주길(to make a product popular) 기대하지만, 글쓴이는 'reach the average consumer directly'해야 한다고 했어요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [keeps them inside a small circle of fellow fans]가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (In other words, their passion [keeps them inside a small circle of fellow fans] rather than spreading to the general public.)
choices: 얼리어답터는 친구가 거의 없다
얼리어답터는 비밀 모임을 만든다
얼리어답터는 신제품을 남에게 빌려주지 않는다
얼리어답터의 열정은 같은 취향의 소수 사이에서만 공유된다
얼리어답터의 열정은 곧 식어 버린다
items.exp: 얼리어답터가 기능을 시험하느라 바빠서 'hardly affect ordinary buyers'라는 내용을 다시 말한 것으로, 그들의 열정이 'the general public'으로 퍼지지 않고 동료 팬들 사이에 머문다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: the most [powerful] shoppers in a market
find better ways to reach the average consumer [indirectly]
a [poor] way to use a limited marketing budget
who know far [less] about technology
businesses should [rethink] any marketing plan
items.exp: 얼리어답터를 거치는 간접 방식이 효과가 없다는 글이므로 일반 소비자에게 '직접(directly)' 다가가야 한다고 해야 맞아요. 원문은 'reach the average consumer directly'예요.

units.name: 08 Design Philosophy
units.passage: Architecture is a form of art. Most people would find it odd that anyone needs to point this out. Yet the philosopher Stephen Davies rejects this idea, even though he admits that a few buildings can be called works of art. In his view, architects put practical function ahead of beauty, and this choice means they cannot be counted as true artists. As a result, he claims that most buildings that architects design are not artworks at all. This is a rather strange position. It rests mainly on the assumption that function and beauty are two totally separate matters. Davies agrees that architects sometimes go beyond mere usefulness, but he still insists that they normally should place function above beauty. However, his reasoning comes from a mistaken either-or way of thinking. In architecture, the useful and the beautiful are naturally woven together. A staircase must carry people safely, but its graceful curve and the light falling on it can also move us. Therefore, the true art of architecture lies in making what is functional beautiful as well.

items.q: 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 건축은 미적 고려보다 기능적 고려를 우선해야 한다.
건축가가 설계한 대부분의 건물은 예술 작품으로 보기 어렵다.
건축가는 기능보다 아름다움만을 추구해야 한다.
건축에서 기능과 아름다움은 서로 얽혀 있으며, 기능적인 것을 아름답게 만드는 것이 건축 예술이다.
현대 건축은 환경에 미치는 영향을 고려해 설계되어야 한다.
items.exp: 글쓴이는 데이비스의 흑백 논리를 반박하며, 쓸모와 아름다움은 함께 엮여 있고 기능적인 것을 아름답게 만드는 것이 건축 예술이라고 말해요.

items.q: 스티븐 데이비스(Stephen Davies)의 생각으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 건축가는 대개 아름다움보다 기능을 우선한다.
모든 건물은 예술 작품이다.
건축가는 결코 쓸모를 넘어서는 작업을 하지 못한다.
기능과 아름다움은 서로 깊이 연결되어 있다.
건축가는 다른 예술가보다 더 뛰어나다.
items.exp: 데이비스는 건축가가 실용적 기능을 아름다움보다 앞에 둔다(put practical function ahead of beauty)고 보았어요. ④는 글쓴이의 생각이에요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 데이비스는 일부 건물은 예술 작품이라고 인정한다.
글쓴이는 데이비스의 입장이 이상하다고 본다.
데이비스의 주장은 기능과 아름다움이 완전히 별개라는 가정에 기초한다.
글쓴이는 계단을 예로 들어 기능과 아름다움이 함께할 수 있음을 보인다.
글쓴이는 데이비스의 양자택일식 사고에 동의한다.
items.exp: 글쓴이는 데이비스의 추론이 잘못된 양자택일식 사고(a mistaken either-or way of thinking)에서 나왔다고 비판해요.

items.q: 지문의 woven together와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: separated
ignored
intertwined
replaced
reduced
items.exp: woven together는 '함께 엮인'이라는 뜻으로, 쓸모와 아름다움이 서로 얽혀 있다는 의미이므로 intertwined와 가까워요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]을 대신할 수 있는 말로 어법상 알맞은 것은?
"...but he still insists that they normally [should place] function above beauty."
choices: placing
place
to place
places
have placed
items.exp: insist가 '~해야 한다'는 당위의 주장을 나타낼 때 that절에는 <(should)+동사원형>을 쓰므로 should를 생략한 place가 알맞아요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Stephen Davies: A Great Philosopher
Function and Beauty: Inseparable in Architecture
Why Buildings Should Be Useful, Not Pretty
How to Design a Safe Staircase
The Decline of Modern Architecture
items.exp: 건축에서 'the useful and the beautiful are naturally woven together'라고 하며 기능과 아름다움을 분리하는 사고를 반박하는 글이에요.

items.q: How would most people react to the statement that architecture is a form of art?
choices: They would strongly disagree with it.
They would ask for scientific proof.
They would think only of famous staircases.
They would agree only if a philosopher said so.
They would find it odd that anyone needs to point it out.
items.exp: 'Most people would find it odd that anyone needs to point this out'이라고 했어요. 즉 대부분은 건축이 예술이라는 것을 당연하게 여겨요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Unlike Davies, who treats usefulness and beauty as (A) ___, the writer argues that architecture's art lies in making functional things (B) ___.
choices: (A) identical — (B) cheap
(A) separate — (B) larger
(A) connected — (B) beautiful
(A) separate — (B) beautiful
(A) equal — (B) safer
items.exp: Davies의 주장은 'function and beauty are two totally separate matters'라는 가정에 기초하고, 글쓴이는 'making what is functional beautiful as well'이 건축 예술이라고 했어요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [go beyond mere usefulness]가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (Davies agrees that architects sometimes [go beyond mere usefulness], but he still insists that they normally should place function above beauty.)
choices: 실용성만이 아니라 아름다움도 추구한다
쓸모없는 건물을 짓는다
건물의 기능을 완전히 무시한다
예산을 초과해서 건물을 짓는다
건물을 필요 이상으로 크게 만든다
items.exp: 'mere usefulness(단순한 쓸모)'를 넘어선다는 것은 기능 외에 아름다움까지 추구한다는 뜻이에요. 그래서 바로 뒤에 but으로 'should place function above beauty'가 이어져요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문장을 옮긴 것으로 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: would find [it] odd that anyone needs to point this out
a few buildings can be [called] works of art
the light [fallen] on it can also move us
most buildings that architects [design] are not artworks at all
rests mainly on the assumption [that] function and beauty
items.exp: 빛이 계단 위에 '떨어지는' 것이므로 능동의 현재분사 'falling'이 명사 light를 꾸며야 해요. 원문은 'the light falling on it can also move us'예요.

units.name: 09 Socratic Wisdom
units.passage: Socrates was truly an unusual thinker, for he declared that the only thing he knew for certain was that he knew nothing. In fact, his usual way of teaching was to ask people what they believed about familiar ideas such as "beauty," "goodness," or "courage." After that, he would use careful reasoning to reveal that their definitions and everyday beliefs contradicted themselves or simply made no sense. Some people of his time considered this method unfair, suspecting that Socrates actually knew more than he admitted. However, his questioning was intended to teach an important lesson: it is dangerous to accept popular beliefs without examining them. He frequently criticized people who claimed to possess sure knowledge about a certain topic. It is mainly because of Socrates that philosophy grew into the modern field of constant critical thinking. What we learn from him is that the greatest threat to both society and each person is to stop thinking critically. When we stop asking questions, we lose the ability to discover our own mistakes.

items.q: 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 통념을 비판 없이 받아들이지 말고 끊임없이 비판적으로 사고해야 한다.
소크라테스는 실제로 많은 것을 알면서 모르는 척했다.
철학은 아름다움과 용기의 정확한 정의를 찾는 학문이다.
논리적인 추론보다 직관을 더 믿어야 한다.
사회적 가치에 무관심한 것이 가장 위험하다.
items.exp: 소크라테스에게서 배우는 것은 사회와 개인에게 가장 큰 위협이 비판적 사고를 멈추는 것이라는 점이라고 했어요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 소크라테스는 자신이 많은 것을 확실히 안다고 말했다.
소크라테스는 주로 긴 강의를 통해 가르쳤다.
당시 일부 사람들은 소크라테스의 방법이 불공정하다고 여겼다.
소크라테스는 특정 주제에 확실한 지식이 있다고 주장하는 사람들을 칭찬했다.
현대 철학은 소크라테스와 거의 관련이 없다.
items.exp: 당시 일부 사람들은 이 방법을 불공정하다(unfair)고 여겼다고 했어요. 그는 질문을 통해 가르쳤고, 확실한 지식을 주장하는 사람들을 비판했어요.

items.q: According to the passage, what was the purpose of Socrates' questioning?
choices: to prove that he was smarter than others
to make people memorize correct definitions
to win arguments in public
to show that courage is more important than beauty
to warn people against accepting common beliefs without examining them
items.exp: 그의 질문은 통념을 따져 보지 않고 받아들이는 것이 위험하다는 교훈을 주려는 것(was intended to teach an important lesson)이었어요.

items.q: 지문의 단어 constant와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: rare
continuous
sudden
careless
final
items.exp: constant critical thinking은 '끊임없는 비판적 사고'라는 뜻이므로 constant는 continuous(계속되는)와 의미가 가까워요.

items.q:
다음 문장과 같은 구문이 쓰인 것은?
"[It is] mainly because of Socrates [that] philosophy grew into the modern field of constant critical thinking."
choices: It is important that you exercise every day.
It was so cold that we stayed at home.
It seems that he is very tired.
It was in the library that I met her.
It is a pity that she can't come.
items.exp: 지문 문장은 because of Socrates를 강조하는 <It is A that ~> 강조구문이에요. 장소 부사구 in the library를 강조한 문장이 같은 구문이에요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: The Life and Death of Socrates
Why Popular Beliefs Are Usually Right
Socrates and the Art of Never Stopping to Question
Beauty, Goodness, and Courage Defined
How Philosophy Lost Its Way
items.exp: 소크라테스에게서 배울 점은 'When we stop asking questions, we lose the ability to discover our own mistakes'라는 것이므로, 끊임없이 질문하는 태도가 제목에 담겨야 해요.

items.q: According to the passage, what did Socrates do after asking people what they believed?
choices: He gave them the correct definitions.
He wrote their answers down in a book.
He praised them for their certainty.
He used careful reasoning to show that their beliefs contradicted themselves or made no sense.
He told them to stop studying philosophy.
items.exp: 질문한 뒤에는 'use careful reasoning to reveal that their definitions and everyday beliefs contradicted themselves or simply made no sense'라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

By exposing the (A) ___ in people's common beliefs, Socrates taught that giving up critical thinking is the greatest (B) ___ to individuals and society.
choices: (A) truth — (B) gift
(A) contradictions — (B) danger
(A) contradictions — (B) benefit
(A) beauty — (B) danger
(A) courage — (B) mystery
items.exp: 그는 사람들의 믿음이 'contradicted themselves'함을 드러냈고, 'the greatest threat to both society and each person is to stop thinking critically'라고 했어요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [the only thing he knew for certain was that he knew nothing]이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (Socrates was truly an unusual thinker, for he declared that [the only thing he knew for certain was that he knew nothing].)
choices: 아무것도 배우지 못했다는 후회
정식 교육을 받지 못했다는 사실
남보다 많이 안다는 자부심
지식은 쓸모가 없다는 믿음
자신의 지식에 한계가 있음을 인정하는 겸손한 태도
items.exp: 'sure knowledge'를 가졌다고 주장하는 사람들을 비판한 소크라테스가 자신은 아는 것이 없다고 선언한 것은, 확실한 지식이란 없음을 인정하는 겸손하고 비판적인 태도를 보여 줘요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: He frequently [praised] people who claimed to possess sure knowledge
his usual way of teaching was to [ask] people
Some people of his time considered this method [unfair]
it is dangerous to [accept] popular beliefs without examining them
we lose the ability to [discover] our own mistakes
items.exp: 확실한 지식을 가졌다고 주장하는 사람들을 그는 '비판했다(criticized)'고 해야 흐름에 맞아요. 원문은 'He frequently criticized people who claimed to possess sure knowledge'예요.

units.name: 10 Art History
units.passage: For centuries, the story of Western art, especially painting, was largely a quest to produce more lifelike pictures. The invention of oil paint allowed artists to create ever more convincing "copies" of the natural world, and many viewers loved works that looked just like a favorite landscape or object. Over the last hundred years or so, however, a number of changes, among them the arrival of photography, have caused the Imitation Theory of art to lose much of its appeal. Once a camera could record a scene perfectly, painters no longer needed to compete with it. From the late 1800s on, many artistic movements, such as impressionism, expressionism, surrealism, and abstract art, have not treated copying reality as their main goal. Nor does the Imitation Theory make space for something we value highly today: an artist's original vision. Are we moved by the irises of Van Gogh or Georgia O'Keeffe because they are exact copies of real flowers? Clearly, that was not what these painters were trying to do, and we admire their flowers for quite different reasons.

items.q: 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: criticism of modern art for its lack of skill
the history of oil painting techniques
why photography completely replaced painting
reasons artists should copy nature exactly
the shift in art's goal from imitation to creative vision
items.exp: 사실적 모방을 추구하던 서양 미술이 사진 등장 이후 모방에서 벗어나 화가의 독창적 시각을 중시하게 되었다는 내용이에요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 유화 덕분에 화가들은 자연을 더 실감 나게 묘사할 수 있었다.
사진의 등장으로 모방 이론의 인기가 더 높아졌다.
많은 사람이 좋아하는 풍경과 똑같아 보이는 그림을 즐겼다.
1800년대 후반부터 여러 미술 사조는 현실 모방을 주된 목표로 삼지 않았다.
글쓴이는 반 고흐와 오키프가 정확한 모방을 목표로 하지 않았다고 본다.
items.exp: 사진의 등장 등 여러 변화로 모방 이론이 매력을 많이 잃었다(lose much of its appeal)고 했어요.

items.q: 글에서 모방 이론(Imitation Theory)의 한계로 언급된 것은?
choices: 그림 재료가 너무 비싸다.
사진보다 정확하게 그릴 수 없다.
풍경화만 예술로 인정한다.
화가의 독창적인 시각이 지닌 가치를 설명하지 못한다.
작품의 가격을 정하는 기준이 없다.
items.exp: 모방 이론은 오늘날 높이 평가하는 화가의 독창적인 시각(an artist's original vision)을 위한 자리가 없다고 했어요.

items.q: 지문의 단어 lifelike의 영영 풀이로 알맞은 것은?
choices: looking very much like the real thing
lasting for a whole lifetime
full of bright colors
painted very quickly
difficult to understand
items.exp: lifelike는 '실물과 똑같은'이라는 뜻으로, 뒤에 나오는 convincing copies of the natural world와 연결돼요.

items.q: 지문의 문장 "Nor [does the Imitation Theory make] space for ..."와 같은 어순 규칙이 바르게 적용된 것은?
choices: I don't like coffee, and nor I do like tea.
She can't swim, and neither can't her brother.
He didn't come to the party, and nor did his sister.
They aren't ready, and nor they are.
We never saw him, and neither we did hear him.
items.exp: nor/neither가 문장 앞에 오면 <(조)동사+주어> 순서로 도치되고, 이미 부정의 뜻이 있으므로 not을 다시 쓰지 않아요. 'nor did his sister'가 맞아요.

items.q: 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Oil paint was the most important invention in art history.
Photography has made painting completely unnecessary.
Van Gogh painted flowers more accurately than any camera could.
Artists today should return to producing lifelike pictures.
Western art has moved away from copying reality toward valuing the artist's own vision.
items.exp: 사진 등장 이후 'the Imitation Theory of art to lose much of its appeal'했고, 오늘날은 'an artist's original vision'을 높이 평가한다는 것이 요지예요.

items.q: According to the passage, why did painters no longer need to compete with the camera?
choices: Because cameras were too expensive for most people.
Because a camera could record a scene perfectly.
Because viewers stopped liking landscapes.
Because oil paint was no longer available.
Because painters began working as photographers.
items.exp: 'Once a camera could record a scene perfectly, painters no longer needed to compete with it'이라고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

For centuries painters sought to (A) ___ nature, but after photography and new art movements appeared, the Imitation Theory lost ground because it ignores an artist's (B) ___.
choices: (A) imitate — (B) income
(A) ignore — (B) originality
(A) imitate — (B) originality
(A) destroy — (B) skill
(A) sell — (B) fame
items.exp: 서양 미술은 'more lifelike pictures'를 추구했지만, 모방 이론은 'an artist's original vision'을 위한 자리를 마련하지 못한다고 했어요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [we admire their flowers for quite different reasons]가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (Clearly, that was not what these painters were trying to do, and [we admire their flowers for quite different reasons].)
choices: 실물과 똑같아서가 아니라 화가의 독창적 시각 때문에 감탄한다
그린 꽃의 종류가 매우 희귀해서 감탄한다
그림이 사진보다 더 정확해서 감탄한다
그림의 가격이 매우 높아서 감탄한다
화가가 꽃을 직접 재배했기 때문에 감탄한다
items.exp: 앞 문장에서 반 고흐와 오키프의 붓꽃이 'exact copies of real flowers'여서 감동하는 것이 아니라고 했으므로, 다른 이유란 'an artist's original vision'을 가리켜요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문장을 옮긴 것으로 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: The invention of oil paint [allowed] artists to create
works that [looked] just like a favorite landscape
the Imitation Theory of art [to lose] much of its appeal
Are we [moving] by the irises of Van Gogh
Once a camera [could record] a scene perfectly
items.exp: 우리가 그림에 의해 '감동을 받는' 것이므로 수동태 'Are we moved by'가 되어야 해요. by 뒤에 감동을 주는 대상이 온 것도 수동태의 단서예요.

units.name: 11 Snapchat
units.passage: Just like traditional video games, social networks and the games and apps that come with them encourage teenagers to become deeply, even obsessively, involved. However, they do so in different ways and lead to different outcomes. For example, when a teenage girl says she has to be on Snapchat, she is not really confessing an addiction; rather, she is expressing a need to stay in touch with her friends. Today, most young people build their identity and social position mainly on the Internet. This makes being online, and taking care of how they appear there, necessary for creating and keeping a place in their real-life relationships. Sherry Turkle, a professor at MIT, explains this point well. According to her, the nervousness teens feel when they are cut off from their phones or the Internet may not show a desire for casual chatting with others. Instead, it may reveal a sense of losing the self that was formed through those connections. In Turkle's view, this is something bigger than addiction, or at least something different from it.

items.q: 글의 요지로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 십 대의 소셜 미디어 사용은 게임 중독과 완전히 같다.
십 대는 소셜 미디어에 자기 정보를 공유하는 데 싫증을 느낀다.
십 대의 소셜 네트워크 몰입은 중독이라기보다 온라인에서 형성된 자아와 관계를 지키려는 것이다.
십 대는 휴대폰 사용 시간을 하루 한 시간 이내로 줄여야 한다.
스냅챗은 다른 앱보다 중독성이 훨씬 강하다.
items.exp: 십 대가 온라인에 있어야 한다고 느끼는 것은 중독이라기보다 사회적 관계와 온라인에서 형성된 자아를 지키려는 필요라는 내용이에요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 소셜 네트워크는 전통적인 게임과 똑같은 결과를 낳는다.
스냅챗을 해야 한다는 소녀의 말은 중독을 고백한 것이다.
오늘날 십 대의 정체성은 주로 오프라인에서 형성된다.
터클은 십 대의 불안이 가벼운 수다에 대한 욕구라고 본다.
셰리 터클은 MIT의 교수이다.
items.exp: Sherry Turkle, a professor at MIT라고 했어요. 소셜 네트워크는 게임과 다른 결과를 낳고, 정체성은 주로 인터넷에서 형성된다고 했어요.

items.q: According to Turkle, what may teens' nervousness show when they are cut off from their phones?
choices: a desire for casual chatting with others
a feeling of losing the self formed through online connections
a fear of missing new games
a wish to spend more time with their families
boredom with social media
items.exp: 터클은 그 불안이 가벼운 대화에 대한 욕구가 아니라 연결 속에서 형성된 자아를 잃는 느낌(a sense of losing the self)을 보여 줄 수 있다고 했어요.

items.q: 지문의 social position에서 position과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?
choices: location
opinion
posture
status
direction
items.exp: identity와 나란히 쓰인 social position은 '사회적 지위'를 뜻하므로 status와 의미가 가까워요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 동사]와 쓰임이 같은 것은?
"This [makes] being online, and taking care of how they appear there, necessary for creating and keeping a place in their real-life relationships."
choices: The sad news made me very upset.
My mom made a cake for us.
He made a lot of money last year.
They made a promise to meet again.
Two and two make four.
items.exp: 지문의 makes는 <make+목적어(being online ...)+형용사 목적격보어(necessary)>의 5형식으로 쓰였어요. 'made me very upset'이 같은 구조예요.

items.q: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Teens Online: Staying Connected, Not Simply Addicted
Snapchat: The Most Dangerous App for Teens
How Video Games Changed Social Networks
Why Teens Should Give Up Their Phones
Sherry Turkle's Career at MIT
items.exp: 십 대가 온라인에 있어야 한다는 것은 'not really confessing an addiction'이고 관계와 자아를 지키려는 필요이며, 터클도 'something bigger than addiction'이라고 했어요.

items.q: In what way are social networks similar to traditional video games, according to the passage?
choices: Both are mainly used alone and offline.
Both lead to exactly the same outcomes.
Both are banned by professors at MIT.
Both encourage teenagers to become deeply involved.
Both help teens avoid their friends.
items.exp: 소셜 네트워크도 전통적인 비디오 게임처럼 'encourage teenagers to become deeply, even obsessively, involved'한다고 했어요. 단, 방식과 결과는 다르다고 했어요.

items.q:
다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Teenagers' strong need to be online is less a sign of (A) ___ than an effort to protect the (B) ___ and relationships they have built through the Internet.
choices: (A) addiction — (B) money
(A) addiction — (B) identity
(A) friendship — (B) identity
(A) boredom — (B) games
(A) laziness — (B) grades
items.exp: 소녀의 말은 중독의 고백이 아니고, 십 대는 'build their identity and social position mainly on the Internet'하므로 온라인에서 만든 자아와 관계를 지키려는 거예요.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [this is something bigger than addiction]이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은? (In Turkle's view, [this is something bigger than addiction], or at least something different from it.)
choices: 십 대의 중독은 어른의 중독보다 훨씬 심각하다
중독은 이제 치료할 수 없을 만큼 커졌다
십 대의 불안은 단순한 중독이 아니라 자아와 관계가 걸린 더 큰 문제이다
십 대는 스냅챗보다 더 큰 앱을 원한다
중독이 오늘날 가장 큰 사회 문제이다
items.exp: 터클은 휴대폰과 단절될 때 느끼는 불안이 'a sense of losing the self that was formed through those connections'를 드러낼 수 있다고 했으므로, 중독보다 큰 문제란 자아와 관계의 문제를 뜻해요.

items.q: 다음 중 글의 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?
choices: encourage teenagers to become deeply, even [obsessively], involved
expressing a need to stay in [touch] with her friends
[necessary] for creating and keeping a place
it may [reveal] a sense of losing the self
the [calmness] teens feel when they are cut off
items.exp: 휴대폰이나 인터넷에서 단절될 때 십 대가 느끼는 것은 '불안(nervousness)'이어야 자아를 잃는 느낌과 연결돼요. 원문은 'the nervousness teens feel when they are cut off'예요.

units.name: 12 Time Management
units.passage: Have you heard of the big-rock experiment? If you want to fill a bucket well, you have to put the big rocks in first and then add the small pebbles. If you try it the other way around, the big rocks will not fit. The lesson is clear: unless you plan your important tasks first, they will never be completed. So when you plan your week, set aside some hours for your big rocks, writing them into your planner. For instance, you might choose Tuesday evening as the best time to begin your history report and Sunday afternoon as the best time to phone your grandmother. Then reserve those times, just as you would book a table at a restaurant. Some big rocks, such as "give three compliments every day this week," may not need a fixed time. In that case, write them somewhere in your planner where you will notice them. Once your big rocks are in place, your smaller daily activities will usually find room as well. And if some of them don't, so what? It is better to leave out a few pebbles than a big rock.

items.q: 글쓴이의 주장으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: 큰일은 작은 일로 나누어 처리하라.
사소한 일을 먼저 끝낸 뒤 중요한 일에 집중하라.
매일 다른 사람을 세 번씩 칭찬하라.
중요한 일에 먼저 시간을 배정하여 일정을 계획하라.
계획표 없이 그때그때 유연하게 생활하라.
items.exp: 중요한 일(big rocks)을 먼저 계획하지 않으면 끝내지 못하므로 주간 계획 때 그 시간부터 확보하라고 주장하고 있어요.

items.q: 큰 돌 실험(the big-rock experiment)에서 양동이를 잘 채우는 방법으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: 큰 돌을 먼저 넣고 그다음에 작은 조약돌을 넣는다.
작은 조약돌을 먼저 넣고 큰 돌을 넣는다.
큰 돌과 조약돌을 섞어서 한꺼번에 넣는다.
조약돌만 가득 넣는다.
양동이를 먼저 물로 채운다.
items.exp: 양동이를 잘 채우려면 큰 돌을 먼저 넣고 그다음 조약돌을 넣어야 하며, 반대로 하면 큰 돌이 들어가지 않는다고 했어요.

items.q: 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 역사 보고서를 시작할 시간으로 화요일 저녁을 예로 들었다.
할머니께 전화할 시간으로 일요일 오후를 예로 들었다.
모든 큰 돌에는 반드시 정해진 시간을 붙여야 한다.
정해진 시간이 필요 없는 일은 계획표의 눈에 띄는 곳에 적어 두라고 했다.
큰 돌을 먼저 배치하면 작은 일들도 대개 들어갈 자리가 생긴다.
items.exp: '세 번 칭찬하기'처럼 정해진 시간이 필요 없는(may not need a fixed time) 큰 돌도 있어서 계획표 어딘가에 적어 두라고 했어요.

items.q: 지문에서 pebbles가 비유적으로 가리키는 것으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: important long-term goals
school history reports
phone calls to family members
weekly planners
small, less important daily activities
items.exp: 큰 돌이 중요한 일이라면 pebbles는 나중에 끼워 넣는 smaller daily activities, 즉 덜 중요한 일상 활동을 가리켜요.

items.q:
다음 문장의 [밑줄 친 부분]과 쓰임이 같은 것은?
"You might choose Tuesday evening as the best time [to begin] your history report."
choices: I went to the store to buy some milk.
I have no time to watch TV today.
To learn a new language is fun.
She was happy to see her old friend.

units.name: 13 Negotiating Skills
units.passage: The first step toward lowering anxiety at the bargaining table is to choose the right topics to discuss. Skilled negotiators avoid putting all their attention on just one point, because talks about a single issue tend to be extremely challenging. When only one matter is being decided, you will probably either hurt your relationship with the other party or walk away with a bad deal. Imagine that you are trying to sell an item and the only thing you talk about is the price. The buyer hopes to pay as little as possible, but the seller hopes to receive as much as possible. In this case, each dollar that one side gains is a dollar that the other side loses. Such talks easily turn into a battle in which one person wins and the other loses. However, when several issues are discussed together, you can discover what each side really cares about. Something that matters a lot to you may mean little to the other person, and the reverse may also be true. This allows both sides to make trade-offs and reach a deal that satisfies everyone.

items.q: 글쓴이의 주장으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
choices: 협상에서는 가격을 먼저 정한 뒤 다른 조건을 논의해야 한다.
협상에서는 한 가지 문제보다 여러 문제를 함께 다루는 것이 좋다.
협상에서는 상대방과의 관계보다 결과를 더 중시해야 한다.
협상에서는 자신이 원하는 것을 끝까지 숨겨야 한다.
협상은 경험이 많은 사람에게 맡기는 것이 안전하다.

물건을 팔 때 구매자와 판매자는 같은 가격을 원한다.

items.q: 가격만 놓고 협상할 때 일어나는 일로 알맞은 것은?

양측 모두 만족하는 거래가 쉽게 이루어진다.

ways of hiding your real goals
giving up one thing in order to gain another

units.name: 14 Decision Making
units.passage: Most people like to think that their choices are usually logical. Economists call this way of choosing utility maximization. First, we estimate how likely each possible result is and how much that result is worth to us. Next, we multiply the chance by the value to find the expected value, or utility, of every choice. Finally, we pick the choice that has the greatest expected utility. However, there is a problem with this picture. Research on how people actually make decisions shows that they rarely follow these steps, especially when gains and losses are involved. People feel the pain of losing something far more strongly than the pleasure of gaining something of equal size. In fact, this feeling is so strong that they will often take risks just to avoid a loss. This is why many investors unwisely hold on to falling stocks, hoping to avoid admitting a loss. It also explains why some drivers keep paying to fix an old car again and again. They see the money they would spend on a new car as a loss, so they hold on to the old one even when replacing it would be the smarter choice.

to forget about a past mistake

units.name: 15 Two-Edged Sword
units.passage: People who have a strong desire to achieve tend to do better than others at earning money. Still, researchers say that this drive can cut both ways. The very ambition that pushes some people toward success can also hurt the way they work. Success at the top of an organization, for instance, often requires a leader to hand over some authority and inspire the people around him or her. Sadly, a person who cares too much about personal achievements may find it hard to let go of small details and trust others to handle them. This could be the reason one study discovered that the need for achievement went along with success among lower managers but not among managers in higher positions. Another case of the same pattern appears in a study of American presidents. Researchers looked at how strongly each president's first official speech showed a need for achievement. Presidents whose speeches revealed a strong need of this kind were generally judged by historians to be fairly weak leaders. In short, a strong need to achieve can help you succeed, but it can also hold you back.

개인적 성취에 더 집중하는 태도

units.name: 16 Polarization
units.passage: These days, people more and more eagerly choose to live among others who share their political views. Conservatives gather in conservative areas, and progressives settle in progressive ones. According to sociologist Robert Cushing and the journalist Bill Bishop, between 1976 and 2008 the share of U.S. counties in which a single presidential candidate won at least 60 percent of the vote almost doubled. When people talked about climate change in their own communities, residents of Boulder shifted further to the left, while residents of Colorado Springs shifted further to the right. This kind of sorting is not limited to politics. It also shapes how people think about social problems, economic policies, and cultural values. In general, people tend to hold more extreme opinions when they belong to a group of like-minded people. The reason is simple: when we hear only from those who agree with us, our views grow stronger and more intense. The Internet makes this problem worse, since it lets anyone find people with the same opinions in a few seconds. As a result, our beliefs become even firmer and harder to change.

units.name: 17 Collective Intelligence
units.passage: Some of the best-known online services were built by ordinary users working together. This 'peer production' gave us eBay, Wikipedia, and MySpace, and it also supplied Netflix with several hundred thousand film reviews. Meanwhile, 'self-service' let Google charge just five cents for each click on an ad and helped Skype gain 60 million members in only two and a half years. In both cases, users willingly do without pay the work that companies would otherwise need to hire staff for. When people click on Google's ads, the company earns money, and every new Skype member makes the service more useful for everyone else. This is not outsourcing but 'crowdsourcing.' Its benefits go beyond saving money, because customers often do the job better. Reviews written by users tend to be knowledgeable and clear, and above all, other users believe them. Taken together, customers have almost endless time and energy, so peer production can reach into every part of every market. With self-service, the job is handled by the people who care about it the most and understand their own needs best. For these reasons, companies should make full use of crowdsourcing.

units.name: 18 AI (Artificial Intelligence)
units.passage: Many people believe false things about artificial intelligence, and these beliefs make them think AI is far more powerful than it really is, both now and in the future. For example, they watch DeepMind's AlphaStar beat top human players at StarCraft II, a game that demands wide-ranging strategy and control of many actions at once. Then they assume that the same computer must be capable of many other smart activities. In reality, however, that game program is narrow AI, just like every other program that people build today. It is made to perform particular jobs, and it cannot apply what it has learned to different fields. There is no possibility that such a program will suddenly decide one day to take over the world. It does not want anything at all; it is simply software. If we clear away these mistaken ideas, we can develop a more realistic view of what AI can and cannot do right now. AI is certainly improving quickly, but we must remember that today's AI systems are highly specialized and work only in the situations they were built for.

units.name: 19 Punctuation
units.passage: Many writers think they are doing their readers a favor when they put a word in quotation marks to show that it is being used in a figurative way. The marks seem to announce, "Careful! This word does not carry its usual meaning here!" In most cases, though, this habit does more harm than good. Readers are usually smart enough to tell when an expression is meant as a metaphor, so these marks, known as scare quotes, only pull their attention away from the message. Take a sentence such as "In this regard, many firms are starting over with a clean slate." No one would imagine that the firms are literally holding a freshly cleaned board. The surrounding words make it obvious that they are simply making a new beginning. Putting quotation marks around "clean slate" adds nothing to the meaning and may even make the writing look awkward. Therefore, writers should drop such unneeded marks. The only time they are worth using is when a figurative phrase is so unusual that readers could not figure out its meaning from the surrounding words.

units.name: 20 Immune System
units.passage: Our immune system works day and night to protect us. It constantly searches the environment for viruses and bacteria, and over time it has built powerful ways to defend the body, cooperating with signals from other body parts. Actually, flexibility matters more to this system than to any other system inside us. If it fails to adjust to the endless variety of threats in a world that never stops changing, we will face serious problems. Surprisingly, however, the same system that guards our health can also be the cause of illness. When it is too weak, germs can easily infect us. On the other hand, when it becomes overly active, it may attack the healthy cells of our own body or overreact to chemicals that are actually harmless. It may also fail to keep ordinary reactions under control, such as the swelling and redness that appear after an injury or during sickness. Obviously, none of these results is good for us. That is why our immune system must stay in balance, neither too weak nor too strong.

units.name: 21 Hope
units.passage: Hope is what keeps us moving. If we had no hope, we would not even begin anything, since we would lack the inner strength needed to work hard and wait patiently for the outcome. Studies support the link between hope and patience. Researchers found that college freshmen with high scores on a hope scale performed better than classmates who had little hope, even though both groups had similar intelligence. The difference came from persistence: hope made the students willing to continue trying. In another experiment, students were asked to imagine a situation. They wanted to get a B in a class, but they received a D on the first exam, which counted for 30 percent of the final grade. What would they do? Students with high hope thought of many different plans to improve their grade, while those with low hope simply quit. So we must remember that being delayed is different from being denied. Not getting what we want right now does not mean we will never get it. Hope helps us survive the hardest moments and grow stronger than before.

units.name: 22 Energy Sources
units.passage: Around the world, people are eager to find huge supplies of clean energy that could reduce the climate crisis caused by the use of coal, oil, and gas. One option that many are looking at is nuclear fusion. This technology could create power while releasing almost no carbon, and unlike the nuclear fission reactors we use now, it would not leave behind dangerous radioactive waste. Scientists have been researching fusion since the 1950s, yet making it work as a usable power source is still very difficult. Most experts believe that fusion will probably not produce energy on a large scale until about 2050, and some even predict 2060. However, how much the planet warms during this century may depend mostly on the actions we take, or fail to take, on carbon emissions in the coming years. For this reason, fusion cannot be a quick answer to the climate crisis. We should not simply wait for it but cut emissions now with the tools we already have.

units.name: 23 Food
units.passage: I strongly support better soil management, including methods such as organic farming. Still, I want to share a view that many people may not like. Almost a billion people suffer from hunger every day, and I do not think organic farming alone can feed all of them. The problem is simply too large, and the places that suffer the most face conditions too harsh for us to depend only on organic methods, which demand a lot of training and very careful management while using only small amounts of fertilizer and seed. Of course, I agree that caring for soil quality matters in every place, from giant corn farms in the United States to the tiny plot of a struggling farmer in Ghana or Guatemala. This work includes many farming techniques that farmers of any size can use in almost any region. In the end, however, to make food secure for those billion people, we will need to use the best methods at many different scales, adjusted to fit local conditions.

units.name: 24 Memory
units.passage: Many people imagine that memories are like sharp video recordings kept safely in the brain, ready to be played back whenever we like. In reality, nothing could be further from the truth. How we feel and what condition our body is in during an event can affect the way we later recall it. Moreover, each time we remember or discuss something from the past, we change the memory a little. We tend to exaggerate the details that fit what we currently believe and how we feel now, and this creates distortions. Memories do not only change in this way; we also select what we keep. This is especially true of our personal histories, which finally form our sense of who we are. We tend to recall the events that support the identity we want most. For example, a person who wants to be seen as a rebel will clearly remember the times he broke the rules but forget the times he obeyed them. On top of that, we can even create completely false memories of events that never took place.

items.exp: 기억이 동영상 같다는 생각은 사실과 거리가 멀며, 기억은 변하고(change), 선택되고(select), 거짓으로 만들어지기도(create false memories) 한다고 했어요.

units.name: 25 Reading
units.passage: Practice leads to skill, but enjoyment is what keeps us practicing. For this reason, choose reading material that you find pleasant. When a book feels so painful that you keep putting it off, close it and find another one that makes you happy. Our time is limited, and good books are everywhere. However, the deepest pleasures usually come from hard work. A book that asks nothing of you may entertain you like a TV comedy show, but it will rarely give your mind or spirit lasting rewards after you finish it. So, while you search for enjoyable books, pick ones that challenge you. Also, read slowly. A delicious dinner should be tasted slowly, and in the same way, a good book deserves full attention rather than a hurried look. Some texts may be fine to read quickly, but skimming all the time harms the mind the way constant fast food harms the body. One critic even warns that speed-reading only tricks you into believing you are learning. Finally, keep a pen or highlighter nearby and write notes as you read. Writing down questions and ideas keeps you active with the text and stops your mind from wandering.

units.name: 26 Climate Change
units.passage: In 2008, the scientist Wallace S. Broecker and the writer Robert Kunzig released a book about climate science titled Fixing Climate. The word "fix" is risky because it sounds quick, simple, and shallow. Is it truly possible for people to repair the climate while they are still damaging it every day? Do we have enough knowledge today to handle it as easily as Kunzig suggests when he says that the earth belongs to us to manage and that we must manage it wisely? History gives us reasons to be careful. Scientists once believed that radiation could cure almost anything, and doctors used mercury to treat many diseases. Both turned out to be harmful. For this reason, we should ask tough questions about the large environmental engineering plans that some climate experts propose. For example, is adding iron to the ocean to grow more plankton really wise? Does it make sense to put huge mirrors in space to send sunlight away from the earth? Before we try to control the whole planet, we must admit how much we still do not know.

items.exp: we should ask tough questions about the large environmental engineering plans라고 하며, 우리가 아직 모르는 것이 많음을 인정해야 한다고 했어요.

units.name: 27 Human Evolution
units.passage: When we look at human evolution, our greatest ability is more than simply learning about the world around us. What truly sets us apart from other animals is our power to imagine other possibilities. This is the real source of the huge advantage humans gained over time. We come to understand the world, and that understanding allows us to dream up and build new worlds. Innovation, technology, and science all grow from this ability. Look around your room right now. You might see a desk with perfectly square corners, electric lamps, and a computer. To an early human living long ago, every one of these objects would seem like something out of a dream. In other words, we are living in a world that we first built inside our heads. Once you see things this way, you understand why we create theories about the world. We make them so that we can picture different ways the world might be, and then we can try to turn those pictures into reality.

units.name: 28 Project Success
units.passage: Once, I spent six weeks training sixteen dancers to perform to a weak musical work titled "The Hollywood Kiss." I did it only because I felt I owed something to the composer, who had helped me before. My dancers were all being paid in full, so I felt I had to give them work. I also felt responsible for the studio I was renting and the people I had employed. Over time, however, I realized that feeling obligated is different from being truly committed. A sense of duty is never a good reason to keep doing something that is failing. So after six weeks without any progress, I finally stopped the project. I had planned everything with great care, and maybe that careful planning was exactly the problem. In the end, I had wasted six weeks for everyone involved. Looking back, I wish I had followed the advice of a CEO I knew. He said that one strong reason is enough to start an idea; you do not need four hundred. But when you have four hundred reasons for yes and a single good reason for no, you should probably say no.

units.name: 29 Rational vs. Emotional
units.passage: Some truths about human psychology are so basic that no textbook is needed to teach them. One of them is this: the stronger our feelings become, the harder it becomes for us to think clearly and act sensibly. Humans are emotional beings by nature. So it would be unrealistic to believe that we could remove our feelings completely, even for a short time during a debate. The goal, then, is not to get rid of emotion altogether but to give reason the most important place. In a good argument, people should be persuaded by its intellectual content, which means the ideas and the way they connect to one another. We should accept a conclusion because we recognize that it is true, not because it makes us feel pleasant. Here is a simple rule to follow: never try to move people by speaking directly to their emotions. Instead, put your energy into guiding them to a point where they can discover the facts on their own. In the end, the truth is the only thing that truly deserves to make us feel good.

units.name: 30 Keystone
units.passage: Biologists know the expression "keystone species" well. It first appeared in 1969 following a study of the seashore by Robert Paine. In his research, Paine took away the purple starfish, a predator, from an area of the shore. As a result, the number of mussels, which the starfish usually ate, exploded, and the variety of living things in the area dropped sharply. A keystone species, then, is a species whose influence is far larger than its population would suggest. The same idea can be applied to people. A keystone species shapes an ecosystem, and in a similar way, "keystone consumers" are a small group of people who shape the market for a certain resource. When just a few users demand too much, plants and animals can be pushed close to disappearing. Water in the U.S. is a good example: farming uses about 80% of it, which makes large farms the keystone consumers. If conservation efforts target these farms, the water supply could recover. Our future depends on both protecting keystone species and cutting back keystone consumption.
